title: Hom objects from the standard simplex and its boundary are the term and the matching object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $K$ a simplicial object of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, with matching objects $M_n(K)$, canonical morphisms $\mu_n:K_n\to M_n(K)$ (components $d_0,\dots,d_n$) and, for $n\geq1$, projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:M_n(K)\to K_{n-1}$ onto the $i$-th factor ($0\leq i\leq n$) [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. For $n\geq0$ let $\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial set with $\Delta[n]_m$ the set of order-preserving maps $\varphi:\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ and $\Delta[n](\psi)(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\psi$, and let $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial subset whose $m$-simplices are the non-surjective $\varphi:\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ (so $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty). For $0\leq i\leq n$ let $\delta_i:\lbrack n-1\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ be the injection omitting $i$, an $(n-1)$-simplex of $\partial\Delta[n]$. Then: (a) $\Delta[n]_m$ is finite and nonempty for all $m$ and $\Delta[n]$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices (the injective $\varphi$), and $K_n$ with the family $(K(\varphi):K_n\to K_m)_{\varphi\in\Delta[n]_m}$ is $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta[n],K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object]: this family is a $\Delta[n]$-family over $K_n$ and every $\Delta[n]$-family $(f_\varphi)$ over an object $W$ is $(K(\varphi)\circ f_{\mathrm{id}_{[n]}})_\varphi$ for the unique morphism $f_{\mathrm{id}_{[n]}}:W\to K_n$. (b) For $n\geq1$, $\partial\Delta[n]_m$ is finite and nonempty for all $m$ and $\partial\Delta[n]$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, and there is a unique isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0\to M_n(K)$ with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\theta=u_{\delta_i}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, where $(u_s)$ is the universal $\partial\Delta[n]$-family. (c) For $n\geq1$, if $\rho:K_n\to\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0$ is the unique morphism with $u_\varphi\circ\rho=K(\varphi)$ for every simplex $\varphi$ of $\partial\Delta[n]$ (the restriction morphism along $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ under the identification (a)), then $\theta\circ\rho=\mu_n$.

proof.text: For each degree, use Mathlib's finite standard-simplex instance and the inherited finite boundary instance. Constant maps give nonempty simplex degrees; for a positive-dimensional boundary, the constant map with value zero misses vertex one, and hence belongs to the boundary in every degree. Mathlib's standard-simplex nondegenerate characterization identifies the nondegenerate simplices with the injective monotone maps. Its finite-simplicial-set instance supplies global finiteness, inherited by the boundary.

proof.text: Construct the standard-simplex family explicitly as K.map of each simplex operator. Functoriality proves compatibility. Evaluate any compatible family at the identity simplex: its compatibility equation gives every other component. This evaluation is inverse to precomposition with the constructed family, so the latter represents the family functor. The identity-component equation also proves the separately stated existence and uniqueness of the morphism.

source.place: Lemma 0177 (lemma-simplex-map), proof: evaluation of a map on the identity simplex

proof.text: For a boundary simplex, use the face-factorization lemma to factor its nonsurjective operator through a codimension-one face. For a compatible tuple of face maps, define its component by composing that face map with K of the factor. If two distinct vertices are omitted, factor again through the face omitting both vertices; the face-face identity and the matching equation identify the two composites. For equal omitted vertices, cancel the monomorphic face map. In degree one all operators into degree zero are equal, and cancellation of their epimorphism gives equality of the omitted vertices. These arguments cover degenerate simplices as well. Apply this construction to the product projections in degree one and the multiequalizer projections in higher degrees. Factorization independence and functoriality prove a boundary family on the concrete matching object. Any boundary family satisfies the matching equations by applying its compatibility to the common codimension-two face; the product or multiequalizer lift therefore supplies a map to that same matching object.

source.place: Lemma 018V (lemma-cosk-shriek), proof via Lemma 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), with the factorization and face relations from Lemmas 0166-0167

proof.text: Given a representing boundary family u on H, lift its codimension-one components into the concrete matching object to obtain a. The universal boundary family on that matching object pulls back along a to u, since both agree on the codimension-one components and factorization determines all components. Representability of u supplies b in the reverse direction. Evaluation of these family equations, injectivity of the representing bijection, and extensionality of matching projections show a followed by b is the identity of H and b followed by a is the identity of the matching object. Thus a and b form the required isomorphism. Its uniqueness follows from the same projection extensionality. This uses the product and multiequalizer APIs directly, without the separate proper-face-category or abstract matching-object theorems.

source.place: Lemma 018V (lemma-cosk-shriek), proof: the boundary Hom object is the degree-n matching object

proof.text: The operators K of boundary simplices form an explicit compatible family on K_(n+1). The representing bijection of u gives the unique restriction morphism rho with all the stated components. For any comparison isomorphism theta with the prescribed face components, compute each matching projection of rho followed by theta: the restriction equation gives K(delta_i), which is the corresponding face map. The concrete matching map has exactly those projections by its product or multiequalizer lift formula. Extensionality of these projections gives rho followed by theta equal to the canonical matching map.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks simplicial.tex Lemmas 0177, 018V and 0186, including the proofs and the face factorization and face relation lemmas 0166-0167. No Lean declaration with this statement exists in WeilConjectures or Comparator. The split writes the finite/nonempty and nondegenerate-simplex checks, proves Hom(Delta[n], K)_0 = K_n by evaluation at the identity simplex, extends compatible codimension-one boundary faces to all non-surjective maps using the existing factorization and face-identity leaves, identifies the resulting functor with the matching object using lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object and lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces, and checks that the restriction map is the matching morphism. No new node was needed because every auxiliary statement is already present in the DAG or is proved explicitly inside a step.
